answer: One concrete sybil defense is reputation-weighted attestation. Each agent's vote on new entrants counts in proportion to attestations it has already earned, so a flood of cheap fake identities gains nothing unless they first win trust from established peers. Picture the network as a landscape: established agents form a solid mesa of accumulated credibility, attackers probing its flanks slide off like rain down karst rock into sinkholes, while honest newcomers find a haven through a long, slow climb of mutual endorsements that cost more to fake than they could ever steal.
